sampling_model.design: Condition on observed \(s\in\mathcal S_T\) and on calibrated, known \(\kappa>0\); require honesty uniformly over the entire observed-share simplex.
sampling_model.units: The observations are the fixed collection of cohort--time totals \(X_{gt}\), not an individual-level sample or a finite-population randomization.
sampling_model.treatment: Cohort \(g\) is untreated for \(t<g\) and treated for \(t\ge g\); the never-treated cohort is indexed by \(\infty\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed cohort share is at least \(1/(2T)\). The exposure, time-effect, and treated-multiplier boxes are separately maintained restrictions on the aggregate-Poisson experiment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Finite-count inference profiles \(A,b,v\) exactly under the product-Poisson likelihood. The high-intensity bridge estimates normalized row and time effects from untreated cells and treated totals. Estimating or jointly calibrating an unknown intensity is not covered.

Minimax expected-measure confidence sets are characterized using Bayes--minimax duality.
Theorem 2 gives Monte Carlo risk convergence, whereas Theorem 6 bounds off-support risk under a density-ratio condition.
The scalar Poisson interval cannot be shortened without lowering infimal coverage below its nominal level.
Auxiliary-uniform randomization splits binomial atoms and yields exact equi-tailed intervals.

body.tldr: A staggered multiplicative panel with rare Poisson totals turns the Moreau--Kastler equation (3.14) proportional-effect setup into a discrete minimax confidence problem. The contribution derives the exact low-intensity deterministic value and all optimizers, proves a strict first-order gain from randomized interval kernels, prices the stronger all-untreated-zero fallback separately, and relates both procedures to the efficient high-intensity Gaussian limit. At every fixed algebraic observed design, stratum-closure continuations reduce strict coverage and risk comparisons, including one-sided membership-switch limits, to finitely many critical-component values. The mandatory \(T=3\), \(\alpha=1/20\), \(\kappa=1/100\), \(K=2\), \(h=1/100\) test is discharged by a globally share-uniform all-\(\Theta\) primal and a complete finite integer lower tree, with a stored integral incumbent and certified gap \(1/20\). The remaining open question is total finite synthesis over arbitrary compact intensity ranges at zero-margin coverage and target-endpoint contacts.

project_justification.gap: Regular staggered-PPML work supplies the proportional target and high-information inference, while exact discrete interval work treats scalar families or finite-prior Monte Carlo approximations. Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, gives Monte Carlo risk convergence and their Theorem 6 gives an off-support density-ratio risk bound; neither it nor qualitative drifting-subsequence asymptotics converts fixed-design strict comparisons into a terminating rational-polyhedral cover valid at all exact contacts.
project_justification.niche: The proved nonregular results determine the low-intensity deterministic and randomized frontier, the separate all-untreated-zero penalty, fixed-algebraic-design strict-comparison reductions, and the high-intensity Gaussian bridge under maintained aggregate-exposure boxes and calibrated known intensity. The paper also gives an exact observed-share-uniform certificate for the mandated sparse \(T=3\) instance. Uniform finite synthesis for arbitrary compact intensity ranges remains open.
project_justification.fill: The paper joins exact low-count values and a high-count efficiency bridge to a rigorous fixed-algebraic-design reduction in which stratum-closure continuations capture attained extrema and unattained membership-switch limits. For the mandatory early-kill instance it explicitly supplies a constant all-\(\Theta\) primal, a two-point endpoint nuisance witness, a stored integral incumbent, a fully indexed multiway integer branch on the zero table, and a rational outward error ledger. The certificate format extends to general ranges, but termination over curved zero-margin contact regions remains the stated open question.

body.related_work: Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), supplies the imputed counterfactual-share proportional target; that algebraic specialization is setup rather than a novel theorem here, and no inclusion of the present aggregate-Poisson class in theirs is claimed. Wooldridge (2023) identifies staggered nonlinear cohort-time effects and makes pooled Poisson quasi-likelihood operational under fixed \(T\), while Martin (2017), Theorems 1--2, establishes regular fixed-\(T\) asymptotics for multiplicative-panel averages; both inform the high-information endpoint. Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005), Theorem 1, supplies Bayes--minimax duality but does not calculate this multivariate connected-interval game. Kabaila and Byrne (2001) supply the ordered scalar exact-Poisson benchmark, Kabaila (2013) supplies auxiliary-uniform atom splitting, and Habiger, McCann, and Tebbs (2013) studies integrated one-parameter discrete optimality. Bochnak, Coste, and Roy (1998) supply the semialgebraic projection, compatible-stratification, finite-component, and path facts used by the fixed-design reduction; the Poisson critical-equation cancellation and discontinuous membership-boundary treatment are derived here. Schafer and Stark (2009), Theorem 2, proves convergence of their Monte Carlo risk calculation, while Theorem 6 bounds off-support risk under a density-ratio condition. Their method does not itself provide the exact specialized early-kill certificate proved here or a terminating continuum-honesty synthesis theorem. Andrews, Cheng, and Guggenberger (2020), Section 2, gives qualitative drifting-subsequence uniformity rather than finite rational cells and machine-checkable enclosures. These comparisons concern different model and action classes, so no strict-strengthening relation is asserted. Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), Theorems 1 and 3, informs the Poisson--Gaussian comparison, but no inclusion of the maintained aggregate-Poisson panel class in their experiment is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fixed-design result does not claim that total coverage is one exponential--polynomial, that the discontinuous piecewise coverage function attains its extrema, or that equality contacts are decidable. It instead optimizes continuous fixed-profile extensions on compact stratum closures and includes unattained one-sided membership-switch limits; outward enclosures terminate only for strict rational comparisons. The mandated \(T=3\), \(\alpha=1/20\), \(\kappa=1/100\), \(K=2\), \(h=1/100\) instance is no longer open: the exact certificate uses the constant all-\(\Theta\) primal and a complete two-point integer lower tree with an integral incumbent. That special proof does not show that arbitrary compact intensity ranges admit a finite rational-polyhedral policy refinement across curved zero-margin contact regions, which is the sole residual certificate obstruction.
body.honest_scope: The causal-functional identity is setup credited to Moreau-Kastler (2025), equation (3.14), and the homogeneous known-mass scalar reduction is a sanity check credited to Kabaila and Byrne (2001). The independent Poisson total law and share lower bound define the experiment; the exposure, time-effect, treatment-effect, and calibrated known-intensity restrictions are maintained rather than consequences of PPML theory. The fixed-algebraic-design separation result covers strict comparisons of closure-continuation extrema and one-sided limits, not exact equality contacts or a uniform finite cover. The early-kill certificate is an exact specialization within this maintained class; it does not establish class inclusion in Moreau--Kastler (2025) or Brown, Carter, Low, and Zhang (2004), nor does it settle total synthesis over arbitrary compact ranges. An unknown or estimated intensity, noninteger outcomes, arbitrary overdispersion, individual-data sufficiency, and software-default intervals remain outside scope.
